OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'

        - firstName

## Summary

I implemented optional, unique email support for owner creation on `POST /api/owners`:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `email` string field to the `OwnerFields` schema (inherited by both `OwnerFieldsDto` and `OwnerDto`, and auto-wired through the MapStruct `OwnerMapper`).

2. **`Owner.java`** — added the `email` column mapping with getter/setter.

3. **DB schemas** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres`) — added a nullable `email VARCHAR(255)` column to the `owners` table.

4. **`hsqldb/data.sql`** — the seed inserts used positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)`; I gave them an explicit column list so the new column doesn't break them (the other dialects already used explicit column lists).

5. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — added an `emailAlreadyExists` check that returns `409 CONFLICT` when a supplied email is already used by another owner. A missing/blank email is ignored, so it never conflicts and is stored/returned as-is.

The new `Cp04Tests` (reject duplicate email → 409, allow missing email, store & return email) all pass, along with the full 264-test suite.
